messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: REAL-TIME ALERT — p99 latency regression detected for streaming.generate on eu-west-1 hosted. p95 jumped from ~120ms -> 480ms, p99 ~2.3s. traffic spike + increased tail variance. Alert threshold crossed at 2026-03-17T09:48:54Z

alice: Ack, seeing the same on the dashboard link: https://console.redwood.example/dashboards/streaming-latency?range=15m

bob: I'm oncall, joining bridge. Starting quick checks: prometheus queries, sampling traces.

sre_jamie: Quick check results: prefix_kv_hitrate down ~15% on average across hosts, eviction spikes at ~09:44. Could be KV cache churn increasing RT.

eng_ops_miguel: Running a repro curl against a couple hosts now: `curl -sS -N https://eu-west-1.api.redwood/v1/stream -H 'Authorization: Bearer <redacted>' -d '{"prompt":"hello"}'` — observed streaming stalls at 1.8s on host runtime-12

alice: Any recent rollout that touched runtime or kvcache config? I see a canary deploy 09:30 that bumped kernel param `kv.max_items` on 10% of fleet.

bob: Good catch. I'm rolling back the canary to 0% on the canary group. Command: `redwoodctl rollout cancel --canary=canary-2026-03-17-0930`

incident-bot: ACTION logged: rollout cancel triggered by bob at 09:52UTC. Notified oncall and eng-ops.

prod_lead_sara: Heads up — we have one enterprise customer on a heavy streaming job. CS is pinged to message them about transient latency. @customer_success_tom can you handle?

customer_success_tom: Pinged the customer, told them we're investigating, offered to shift their workload to Dedicated if they want immediate relief. They asked for ETA ~15-30m.

eng_ops_miguel: While rollback goes, enabling fallback routing to dedicated pool for streaming.generate for 10% traffic: `redwoodctl routing set --route streaming.generate --policy fallback:dedi-eu-1 --pct 10`

alice: Also enabling temporary aggressive batching tuning to reduce tail: set `batch.max_delay_ms=8` for streaming routers in eu-west-1. Command: `redwoodctl config set router.batch.max_delay_ms=8 --region eu-west-1`

bob: Observing metrics after rollback + routing change: p95 down from 480ms -> 210ms over last 3 mins, p99 from 2.3s -> 700ms. Still above SLO but improving.

sre_jamie: I pulled a few traces, root cause indicators look like repeated cache misses causing repeated KV refill work during the sequence leading to stalls. Candidate RCA: canary tuned `kv.max_items` too low -> increased evictions -> hot-prefix thrashing.

prod_lead_sara: Good work. Plan: keep rollback + 10% fallback for 30m, monitor p95/p99 and customer impact, then fully rollback canary and revert config change. If p99 doesnt stabilize, escalate to full traffic fallback and consider model-quantized variant for short term.

bob: Assigning follow-ups: alice to validate rollback completed and config reverted (10m), miguel to watch fallback routing and scale dedicated pool if saturation appears (ongoing), jamie to assemble trace samples for postmortem (after stable).

alice: Confirming canary rollback reached 100% cancel at 09:56UTC, config revert queued.

eng_ops_miguel: Dedicated pool usage increased by 8% after routing change, no saturation yet. I bumped dedi-eu-1 by +2 nodes as buffer.

incident-bot: NOTE: customer-impact flag = partial degradation; pages escalated to Sev-2 per SLO policy.

customer_success_tom: Customer acknowledged temporary mitigation and is OK with monitoring updates every 15 minutes.

bob: Closing initial triage. Next: monitor for 30m, if p99 >1s re-open and route 50% to dedi and enable quantized model variant. Will follow up with postmortem once stable. :white_check_mark:
